**Moraes Schedules Trial of Former DF Military Police Leadership for Omission in January 8 Attacks**

Relator Minister Alexandre de Moraes opened the voting on November 7, 2025, casting a vote that rejected all defense arguments and reaffirmed Bolsonaro’s 27-year and 3-month prison sentence. Moraes reiterated that Bolsonaro led an 'armed criminal organization' aimed at restricting constitutional powers and attempting the violent overthrow of a legally constituted government. According to journalist Robson Bonin, no one within the STF or among defense lawyers believes the verdict will be reversed, calling the outcome 'a consolidated picture' with no possibility of reversal. With Minister Luiz Fux having been transferred to the Second Chamber, the decision now requires unanimous confirmation by four ministers. José Benedito da Silva of VEJA stated that Bolsonaro is experiencing his most politically fragile moment since the conviction, having lost political support even within the right-wing spectrum. The right has shifted focus to public security as a new mobilization platform, rendering Bolsonaro obsolete in street protests and social media influence. The previously discussed amnesty agenda has been abandoned, with no one now mentioning it. The defense’s current strategy is to delay proceedings through procedural motions like declarations of clarification and dilatory appeals, potentially pushing the final judgment into the judicial recess from December to January 2026. This would aim to delay prison execution until the 2026 election year, when political conditions might favor Bolsonaro—though such a move is deemed unlikely. Despite minimal chances, the STF is expected to confirm the sentence’s enforcement this year. Bolsonaro is anticipated to serve a few days in closed regime, possibly at Papuda Prison in Brasília, before obtaining house arrest due to health reasons, similar to Fernando Collor. 'It’s a bad moment for Bolsonaro. Politically, he’s weakened. Legally, there’s no way out,' concluded José Benedito.

The case concerning former TSE (Superior Electoral Court) advisor Tagliaferro, accused of leaking confidential messages, is under review by Brazil's Supreme Federal Court (STF) First Turma, led by Minister Alexandre de Moraes. The confirmation of Carlos Bolsonaro's pre-candidacy for the Senate in Santa Catarina for the 2026 elections has triggered a rift within the local branch of the PL (Liberal Party). Italy’s judiciary will assess whether the acts constitute a crime under Article 326 of the Italian Penal Code (revelation of official secrets), while the defense claims political persecution and bias, as Moraes is both victim and judge. The hearing will also evaluate whether the process respects fundamental rights, which may influence the extradition decision. Despite the federal government leading the CPI under Senator Fabiano Contarato (PT-ES), senators Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) and Hamilton Mourão (Republicans-RS) are actively inviting governors and security secretaries from low-violence states to testify. The CPI will also hear from federal and state authorities and investigate the operations of criminal factions and militias nationwide. The program 'Sem Rodeios' on November 6, 2025, will feature state deputy Ana Campagnolo (PL-SC), Tagliaferro’s lawyer with updates on the Italian case, and pastor Silas Malafaia for a frank political discussion.
